title: The German Bavarian Board
seo_title: German Charcuterie Board: Oktoberfest Shopping List
description: A Bavarian beer-hall board for 8–10: warm Weisswurst, Obatzda, smoked cheese, Landjäger, soft pretzels and sweet mustard. What to buy and how to serve it.
hook: An Oktoberfest spread built the way Munich beer gardens do it: warm sausage, soft pretzels, a bowl of Obatzda and two kinds of mustard.
why: Bavarian beer-hall food is all about salt, fat and something sharp to cut it. Weisswurst is a mild, fresh veal-and-pork sausage that is poached and served warm, so it gets its own bowl of hot water and a pot of sweet mustard beside it. Landjäger and Black Forest ham bring smoke and chew, and the spicy brown mustard is there for them.

The cheeses cover three textures: firm, smoky Räucherkäse, nutty Emmentaler and creamy Obatzda, a paprika-spiked Camembert spread made for pretzels. Cornichons and peppery radishes, a Bavarian beer snack in their own right, cut the richness, and green grapes add a sweet, fresh bite.

timeline.what: Take the cheeses and cured meats out of the fridge.
Slice the Emmentaler, radishes and grapes.
Poach the Weisswurst and warm the pretzel bites.
Fill ramekins with Obatzda, mustards and honey.
Arrange the board, add the Weisswurst in hot water, and scatter chives.

faq.q: Where can I buy Weisswurst and Obatzda?
faq.a: German delis and butchers often carry fresh Weisswurst, and some large grocery stores stock it near the bratwurst. Obatzda is easy to make: mash ripe Camembert with soft butter, sweet paprika, finely chopped onion and a splash of beer.
No. Weisswurst is a fresh sausage that is gently poached and served warm. Guests peel off the casing and eat it with sweet mustard and a pretzel.

faq.q: What beer goes with a Bavarian board?
faq.a: A Märzen or Oktoberfest lager is the classic choice. Weissbier suits the Weisswurst and pretzels, and a dark Dunkel works well with the smoked cheese.
Make the Obatzda up to a day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge. Slice the cheese and prep the radishes a few hours before, but poach the Weisswurst and warm the pretzels right before serving.
